label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The classroom is recognizable: repeated wooden desks and benches, yellow lower walls, tall side openings, ceiling fans, bags, and the curtained stage with a board are present.
Desk rows flank a central aisle leading to the stage; side openings and overhead fans preserve the main spatial relationships. Placement is more regular than the reference.
Desks, benches, bags, board, and fans have broadly plausible relative sizes within the room, despite slender furniture and generous spacing.
Cream and yellow walls, brown furniture, blue and dark bags, green board and side curtains, and a dark burgundy backdrop retain the main color organization. Surfaces are simplified and pale.
The bright interior remains legible with coherent soft shadows and bright side windows. Lighting is flatter than the reference and rendering is noisy, but major content is visible.
Complementary views show furniture tops, sides, legs, and changing occlusions within a volumetric room, establishing a genuine three-dimensional reconstruction.
Actual mesh records provide editable architecture, desk parts, seating, board, and bags, with finite nonempty geometry, parent chains, and assigned node materials. The scene contains 388 meshes.

dimension_scores.evidence: Strongly recognizable classroom identity and major features, with less architectural detail, simpler furniture, and a more orderly arrangement.
Desks generally meet the floor, but benches have only two narrow central supports. Board supports end above the platform, and door panels begin well above floor level.
The main palette corresponds well, but yellow walls and brown furniture look washed out; bags and curtains use very basic silhouettes.
Heavy grain, uniform block furniture, flat curtain panels, blank windows, and ellipsoidal bags make the scene read as a rough model.
The long room, central aisle, stage destination, and side furniture are preserved. Rows are unusually uniform, and seats are only provided for the central desk columns.
Most major size relationships are plausible, though furniture supports are thin, benches are narrow, and the room feels more spacious around the furniture.
Soft light makes the room readable, but weak directional contrast, persistent noise, and nearly uniform surface response lose the reference's material variation and darker furniture.
Major architecture, numerous desks and benches, fans, bags, speakers, and stage elements are included. Peripheral seating, furniture detailing, and opening details are reduced.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
